To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the revised modified DAINMOD shallow wtd approach in SWAT can accurately simulate wtd at the field scale, and (2), when the variable wt_fctr is used, the revised modified DRAIMOD shallow wtd approach can accurately simulate wdt at the watershed scale.

the revised modified DAINMOD shallow wtd approach in SWAT can be used to automatically compute the variable water table factor (wtfctr) as a function of the soil physical properties and the wtd algorithm can be applied to the watershed scale.

the revised shallow water table depth algorithm that uses automatically computed variable water table factor values yielded similar model performance results to the original shallow water table depth model that used manually calibrated constant water table factor values for the Muscatatck River basin in southeast IN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the simulation of shallow water table depth in the Soil and Water Assesment Tool.
the development of a new shallow wtd algorithm in a hydrologic model that is more realistic and more easily applied at the watershed scale.
the incorporation and validation of the revised modified DAINMOD wtd algorithm into the SWAT model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the revised modified DRAINDMOD shallow wtd approach, which automatically computes the wt_fctr, is an improvement over the previous version of the algorithm in SWAT.
the revised modified DAINMOD shallow wtd approach in SWAT is capable of accurately simulating shallow wtd at the field and watershed scales.
the revised modified DAINMOD approach in SWAT is an effective and accurate shallow wtd model that can be used to simulate wtd at both the field and watershed scales.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to develop a revised shallow wtd algorithm that will allow the SWAT model to simulate wtd without the need to manually calibrate the constant wt_fctr.
the revised modified DRAIMOD wtd algorithm can be applied to the entire Muscatatuck watershed and the automatically computed wt_fctr can be used to simulate the wtd at any field within the watershed.
we have developed a shallow wtd algorithm that will be useful for SWAT users who want to simulate wtd at the watershed scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the revised modified DRAIMMOD shallow wtd model can be used to simulate wtd in forested watersheds where wtd can be measured.
the automatically computed variable water table factor (WT_FCTR) can be used to simulate water table depth in SWAT.
the revised modified DAINMOD approach is a good option for SWAT users to simulate wtd.
